notes.largest_clone_class: 118 regions a player cannot tell apart. G4 counts these once, not 118 times.
notes.wallpaper_locations: Rooms with no verb of their own. PLAN.md: 'Empty miles are a disqualification.'
notes.worst_hub_cut_fraction: Removing one location strands this fraction of the world. G1 wants one contiguous world, not a hub with pockets.
notes.sheet_gated_outcome_actions: G3 asks the sheet to change what you can achieve. Exactly 1 action does that (`sign_the_compact`: an oathbound creed signs without dock standing) against 143 outcome-gating flags. The other 311 sheet-gated actions only change which verb is printed; both branches set the same flag.
notes.unused_effect_ops: Implemented verbs the world never calls. `hurt` unused means nothing can go wrong anywhere.
notes.unused_condition_kinds: `remembers` unused means 566 NPC memory writes are read by nobody.

not_measured.g2_plain_speech: G2 asks for plain speech. `verify/language.py` enforces SHORT speech: 20-word sentences, 8-word labels, 7 banned phrases. 'Woold bowsprit, ride turns, frap gammon' passes every one of them. A glossary heuristic was tried and rejected: scoring label words against the region's own prose ranks the generated clones BEST (they echo their jargon back: 'Pillar says hew the pillar') and the hand-authored regions WORST, so it would have punished the good writing. Detecting jargon needs a real word-frequency list; until then this gap is open and is not silently counted as passing.
